title: The nature of continuity and change
log: 2026-10-29T12:14:28Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: The nature of continuity and change
card: something that stays much the same over time, such as a language, a belief or a custom.
something that becomes different over time, such as how people work, travel or communicate.
Most societies show both at once. A society can change some parts of life and keep others.
Studying one country across a long period shows how tradition and change shape each other. A custom may be kept, adapted or dropped as life around it changes.
draft.remember: Societies rarely only change or only stay the same. Both happen together.

a.q: Which statement best describes how most societies change over time?
opts: They change some parts of life and keep others
They change every part of life at the same pace
They keep all traditions once they are established
They drop tradition completely when a change begins
a.why: Most societies show continuity and change together, so some parts shift while others stay. The idea that everything changes at once is tempting, but it ignores the customs and beliefs that people keep.
a.clue: Think about both things happening in one society.

b.q: A family in Bali still holds a yearly temple ceremony as their grandparents did. They now share photos of it on their phones. What does this show?
opts: Continuity in the ceremony and change in how it is shared
Change in the ceremony and continuity in how it is shared
Continuity in both the ceremony and how it is shared
Change in both the ceremony and how it is shared
b.why: The ceremony stays much the same, so that is continuity. Sharing photos on phones is a new way of communicating, so that is change. The reversed option swaps the two parts.
b.clue: Ask which part is the same as before and which part is new.

a.best: They change some parts of life and keep others

b.best: Continuity in the ceremony and change in how it is shared
